audioscript.text: Section 1.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear a telephone conversation between an official at a village hall and a woman who wants to hire a public room.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will see that there is an example that has been done for you.

audioscript.text: Hello?
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Oh hello, I wanted to inquire about hiring a room in the village hall for the evening of September the first.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Let me just see.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Uh. Yes, we have both rooms available that evening.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: There's our Main Hall, that's got seating for 200 people.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Or there's the Charlton Room.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: The Main Hall seat's 200, so 200 has been written in the space.

audioscript.text: Hello?
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Oh hello, I wanted to inquire about hiring a room in the village hall for the evening of September the first.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Let me just see.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Uh. Yes, we have both rooms available that evening.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: There's our Main Hall, that's got seating for 200 people.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Or there's the Charlton Room.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Sorry?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: The Charlton Room, CHARLTON.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q1: The passage says *'The Charlton Room, CHARLTON'* and *'That's got seating for up to 100'*. The question asks for the room that seats 100, so the answer is **Charlton**.

audioscript.text: That's got seating for up to 100.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q1: The passage says *'The Charlton Room, CHARLTON'* and *'That's got seating for up to 100'*. The question asks for the room that seats 100, so the answer is **Charlton**.

audioscript.text: Well, we're organizing a dinner to raise money for a charity, and we're hoping for at least 150 people.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: So, I think we'll go for the Main Hall.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: How much would that cost?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Let's see, um, you wanted it for the evening of September the first.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Yes, that's a Saturday.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: So from 6 pm to midnight, that would be £115 that's the weekend price.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q2: The passage says *'that would be £115 that's the weekend price'*. The question asks for the cost of the Main Hall on a Saturday, which is a weekend. So the answer is **115**.

audioscript.text: It's £75 on weekdays.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: That's all right.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: And I have to tell you there's also a deposit of £250 which is returnable of course, as long as there's no damage.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: But we do insist that this is paid in cash.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q3: The passage says *'we do insist that this is paid in cash'* about the deposit. The question asks what payment is required for the deposit. So the answer is **cash**.

audioscript.text: We don't take cards for that.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: You can pay the actual rent of the room, however you like though.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Cash, credit card, cheque...
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Oh, well, I suppose that's OK.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: So does the charge include use of tables and chairs and so on?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Oh, yes.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: And what about parking?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Yeah, that's all included.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q4: The woman asks *'what about parking?'* and the man says *'that's all included'*. The question asks what else is included with the cost. So the answer is **parking**.

audioscript.text: The only thing that isn't included is... you said you were organizing a dinner.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Yeah.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Well, you'll have to pay extra for the kitchen if you want to use that.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: It's got very good facilities, good quality cookers and fridges and so on.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: OK, well I suppose that's all right.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: We can cover the cost in our entry charges.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Right, so I'll make a note of that.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Now, there are just one or two things you need to think about before the event.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: For example, you'll have to see about getting a license if you're planning to have any music during the meal.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q5: The passage says you need a license *'if you're planning to have any music'*. The question asks what kind of license is needed. So the answer is **music**.

audioscript.text: Oh, really?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: It's quite straightforward.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: I'll give you the details later on.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: And about a week or 10 days before your event, you'll need to contact the caretaker, that's Mr Evans.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q6: The passage says to contact the caretaker *'to make the arrangements for entry'*. The question asks what you need to arrange with him. So the answer is **entry**.

audioscript.text: Uh. To make the arrangements for entry, he'll sort that out with you.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q6: The passage says to contact the caretaker *'to make the arrangements for entry'*. The question asks what you need to arrange with him. So the answer is **entry**.

audioscript.text: And do I give him the payment as well?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: No, you do that directly with me.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Right, now is there anything I need to know about what happens during the event?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Well, as you'll be aware, of course, the building is no smoking throughout.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Of course.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Now are you having a band?
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Yes.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Well, they'll have a lot of equipment, so rather than using the front door, they should park their van round the back, and use the stage door there.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q7: The passage says the band should *'use the stage door there'* at the back. The question asks which door the band should use. So the answer is **stage**.

audioscript.text: You can open that from inside, but don't forget to lock it at the end.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: OK.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: And talking of bands, I'm sure I don't need to tell you this, but you must make sure that no one fiddles about with the black box by the fire door.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: That's a system that cuts in when the volume reaches a certain level, it's a legal requirement.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Sure.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Anyway, we want people to be able to talk to one another.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: So we don't want anything too loud.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Oh, that reminds me, we'll be having speeches.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Are there any microphones available?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Yeah.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Just let the caretaker know, he'll get those for you.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Right, now when the event is over, we do ask that the premises are left in good condition.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: So there's a locked cupboard, and you'll be informed of the code you need to open that.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q8: The passage says *'you'll be informed of the code you need to open that'* for the locked cupboard. The question asks what you need to know for the cleaning cupboard. So the answer is **code**.

audioscript.text: It's got all the cleaning equipment, brushes and detergent and so on.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: Right, so what do we need to do after everyone's gone?
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Uh. Sweep the floors, I suppose.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Well, actually they have to be washed, not just swept.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q9: The passage says *'they have to be washed, not just swept'* about the floors. The question asks what must be washed. So the answer is **floors**.

audioscript.text: Then you'll be provided with black plastic bags, so all the rubbish must be collected up and left outside the door.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q9: The passage says *'they have to be washed, not just swept'* about the floors. The question asks what must be washed. So the answer is **floors**.

audioscript.text: Of course, we'll make sure everything's left tidy.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Oh, and I forgot to ask.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: I presume we can have decorations in the room.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: Yes, but you must take them down afterwards.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL
audioscript.explain: Q10: The woman asks about decorations and the man says *'you must take them down afterwards'*. The question asks what must be taken down. So the answer is **decorations**.

audioscript.text: Sure.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: And the chairs and tables should be stacked up neatly at the back of the room.
audioscript.speaker: OFFICIAL

audioscript.text: I'll make sure I've got a few people to help me.
audioscript.speaker: WOMAN

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 1.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Section 2.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear a guide talking to a group of visitors to a farm.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Listen carefully, and answer questions 11 to 14.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Welcome to the Fiddy Working Heritage Farm.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: This open air museum gives you the experience of agriculture and rural life in the English countryside.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: At the end of the 19th century.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So you'll see a typical farm of that period, and like me, all the staff are dressed in clothes of that time.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: I must give you some advice and safety tips before we go any further.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As it's a working farm, please don't frighten or injure the animals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q11: The guide says *'please don't frighten or injure the animals'* — **'injure'** means **'harm'**. So you must not harm any **animals**.

audioscript.text: We have a lot here, and many of them are breeds that are now quite rare.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And do stay at a safe distance from the tools.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Some of them have sharp points, which can be pretty dangerous, so please don't touch them.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q12: The guide warns that some tools *'have sharp points'* and says *'please don't touch them'*. So you must not touch any **tools**.

audioscript.text: We don't want any accidents, do we?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The ground is very uneven, and you might slip if you're wearing sandals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So I'm glad to see you're all wearing shoes.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q13: The guide says *'I'm glad to see you're all wearing shoes'* and *'We always advise people to do that'*. So you should wear **shoes**.

audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear two psychology students called Lisa and Greg discussing a project they have to do.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 27.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 21 to 27.

audioscript.text: OK, Greg.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: So I finally managed to read the article you mentioned, the one about the study on gender in physics.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: About the study of college students done by Akira Miyake and his team?
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Yeah, I was interested that the researchers were actually a mix of psychologists and physicists.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: That's an unusual combination.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Yeah.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: I got a little confused at first about which students the study was based on.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: They weren't actually majoring in physics, they were majoring in what's known as the STEM disciplines.
audioscript.speaker: LISA
audioscript.explain: Q21: The passage says the students *'weren't actually majoring in physics'* — instead, they were in **'STEM disciplines'**. Then it explains **STEM** means *'science, technology, engineering, and... math'*. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: That's science, technology, engineering, and...
audioscript.speaker: LISA
audioscript.explain: Q21: The passage says the students *'weren't actually majoring in physics'* — instead, they were in **'STEM disciplines'**. Then it explains **STEM** means *'science, technology, engineering, and... math'*. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: ...and math.
audioscript.speaker: GREG
audioscript.explain: Q21: The passage says the students *'weren't actually majoring in physics'* — instead, they were in **'STEM disciplines'**. Then it explains **STEM** means *'science, technology, engineering, and... math'*. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Yes, but they were all doing physics courses as part of their studies.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: That's correct.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: So, as I understood it, Miyake and co started from the fact that women are underrepresented in introductory physics courses at college.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: And also that on average, the women who do enroll on these courses perform more poorly than the men.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: No one really knows why this is the case.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Yeah, but what the researchers wanted to find out was basically what they could do about the relatively low level of the women's results, but in order to find a solution.
audioscript.speaker: GREG
audioscript.explain: Q22: The passage says the researchers wanted to find *'what they could do about the relatively low level of the women's results'* — **'what they could do'** means finding a way to improve performance. So the aim was **a way of improving women's performance in physics**, which is **B**.

audioscript.text: They needed to find out more about the nature of the problem.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Right.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Now let's see if I can remember, it was that in the physics class, the female students thought the male students all assumed that women weren't any good at physics.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Was that it?
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: And they thought that the men expected them to get poor results in their tests.
audioscript.speaker: LISA
audioscript.explain: Q23: The passage says the female students *'thought that the men expected them to get poor results in their tests'*. This directly matches option **B** — the male students expected them to do badly. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: That's what the women thought, and that made them nervous, so they did get poor results.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: But actually they were wrong.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: No one was making any assumptions about the female students at all.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Anyway, what Miyake's team did was quite simple.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Getting the students to do some writing before they went into the physics class.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: What did they call it?
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Values-affirmation.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: They had to write an essay focusing on things that were significant to them.
audioscript.speaker: GREG
audioscript.explain: Q24: The passage says the students wrote about *'things that were significant to them'* — **'significant'** means **'important personally'**. It gives examples like *'music or people who mattered to them'*, not physics. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Not particularly to do with the subject they were studying, but more general things like music or people who mattered to them.
audioscript.speaker: GREG
audioscript.explain: Q24: The passage says the students wrote about *'things that were significant to them'* — **'significant'** means **'important personally'**. It gives examples like *'music or people who mattered to them'*, not physics. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Right.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: So the idea of doing the writing is that this gets the students thinking in a positive way.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: And putting these thoughts into words can relax them and help them overcome the psychological factors that lead to poor performance.
audioscript.speaker: GREG
audioscript.explain: Q25: The passage explains the writing *'can relax them and help them overcome the psychological factors that lead to poor performance'*. **'Relax'** and **'overcome psychological factors'** both mean **to reduce stress**. So the aim was to reduce stress, which is **A**.

audioscript.text: Yeah.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: But what the researchers in the study hadn't expected was that this one activity raised the women's physics grades from the C to the B range.
audioscript.speaker: GREG
audioscript.explain: Q26: The passage says the researchers *'hadn't expected'* that the activity *'raised the women's physics grades from the C to the B range'*. This was a **positive impact** on women's results that surprised them. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: A huge change.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Pity it wasn't to an A, but still!
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: No, but it does suggest that the women were seriously underperforming beforehand in comparison with the men.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Yes.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Mind you, Miyake's article left out a lot of details, like did the students do the writing just once or several times, and had they been told why they were doing the writing?
audioscript.speaker: GREG
audioscript.explain: Q27: The passage mentions Miyake's article left out details like *'had they been told why they were doing the writing?'*. This is about **the information the students were given** — if they knew the purpose, it might change results. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: That might have affected the results.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: You mean if they know the researchers thought it might help them to improve, then they'd just try to fulfill that expectation?
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Exactly.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 28 to 30.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 28 to 30.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: So anyway, I thought for our project we could do a similar study, but investigate whether it really was the writing activity that had that result.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: OK, so we could ask them to do a writing task about something completely different, something more factual, like a general knowledge topic.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Maybe, or we could have half the students doing a writing task, and half doing something else like an oral task.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Or even, half do the same writing task as in the original research, and half do a factual writing task.
audioscript.speaker: LISA
audioscript.explain: Q28: The passage says they will compare *'half do the same writing task as in the original research, and half do a factual writing task'*. These are **two different writing tasks** — one personal, one factual. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: Then we'd see if it really is the topic that made the difference, or something else.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: That's it.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Good.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: So, at our meeting with the supervisor on Monday, we can tell him we've decided on our project.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: We should have our aims ready by then.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: I suppose we need to read the original study.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: The article is just a summary.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: And there was another article I read by Smolinsky.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: It was about her research on how women and men perform in mixed teams in class,
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: compared with single-sex teams and on their own.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Let me guess... the women were better at teamwork.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: That's what I expected, but actually the men and the women got the same results.
audioscript.speaker: LISA
audioscript.explain: Q29: The passage says *'the men and the women got the same results'* whether in teams or alone. This means teamwork had **no effect on performance** for either group. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: Whether they were working in teams or on their own.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Hmm. But I guess it's not that relevant to us.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: What worries me anyway is how we're going to get everything done in the time.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: We'll be OK, now we know what we're doing.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Though, I'm not clear how we assess whether the students in our experiment actually make any progress or not.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: No, we may need some advice on that.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: The main thing's to make sure we have the right size sample, uh, not too big or too small.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: That shouldn't be difficult.
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Right, what do we need to do next?
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: We could have a look at the timetable for the science classes, or perhaps we should just make an appointment to see one of the science professors.
audioscript.speaker: LISA
audioscript.explain: Q30: The passage suggests *'make an appointment to see one of the science professors'* and Lisa says *'That'd be better'*. So their next step is to **talk to a professor**, which is **A**.

audioscript.text: That'd be better.
audioscript.speaker: LISA
audioscript.explain: Q30: The passage suggests *'make an appointment to see one of the science professors'* and Lisa says *'That'd be better'*. So their next step is to **talk to a professor**, which is **A**.

audioscript.text: Great.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: And we could even get to observe one of the classes.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: What for?
audioscript.speaker: LISA

audioscript.text: Well, OK, maybe let's just go with your idea.
audioscript.speaker: GREG

audioscript.text: Right, well, I think that's everything for now.

audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear part of a student presentation about the variety of different species that live in the world's oceans.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully, and answer questions 31 to 40.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: I've been looking at ocean biodiversity.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That's the diversity of species that live in the world's oceans.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: About 20 years ago, biologists developed the idea of what they called biodiversity hotspots.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: These are the areas which have the greatest mixture of species, so one example is Madagascar.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: These hotspots are significant.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Because they allow us to locate key areas for focusing efforts at conservation.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q31: The passage says hotspots help us *'locate key areas for focusing efforts at conservation'*. The question asks what hotspots are important for locating targets for — **'conservation'** is the exact word from the passage. So the answer is **conservation**.

audioscript.text: Biologists can identify hotspots on land fairly easily.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But until recently, very little was known about species distribution and diversity in the oceans, and no one even knew if hotspots existed there.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Then a Canadian biologist called Boris Worm did some research in 2005 on data on ocean species that he got from the fishing industry.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Worm located five hotspots for large ocean predators like sharks, and looked at what they had in common.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The main thing he'd expected to find was that they had very high concentrations of food.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But to his surprise, that was only true for four of the hotspots.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: Worm expected hotspots to have high concentrations of food, but the passage says *'that was only true for four of the hotspots'* and the rest were *'quite badly off in that regard'*. **'In that regard'** refers back to **'food'**. So the answer is **food**.

audioscript.text: The remaining hotspots were quite badly off in that regard.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: Worm expected hotspots to have high concentrations of food, but the passage says *'that was only true for four of the hotspots'* and the rest were *'quite badly off in that regard'*. **'In that regard'** refers back to **'food'**. So the answer is **food**.

audioscript.text: But what he did find was that in all cases, the water at the surface of the ocean had relatively high temperatures.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q33: The passage directly states Worm found *'the water at the surface of the ocean had relatively high temperatures'*. The question asks where the higher temperatures were — at the **surface**. So the answer is **surface**.

audioscript.text: Even when it was cool at greater depths, so, this seemed to be a factor in supporting a diverse range of these large predators.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: However, this wasn't enough on its own, because he also found that the water needed to have enough oxygen in it.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q34: The passage says besides temperature, the water *'needed to have enough oxygen in it'*. The question asks what the water had sufficient — **'oxygen'** is the exact word. So the answer is **oxygen**.

audioscript.text: So these two factors seem necessary to support the high metabolic rate of these large fish.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: A couple of years later, in 2007, a researcher called Lisa Balance, who was working in California, also started looking for ocean hotspots.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But not for fish.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: What she was interested in was marine mammals, things like seals.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: Lisa Ballance was interested in *'marine mammals, things like seals'*. The question asks what type of marine life she looked for hotspots for — **'mammals'** is the direct answer. So the answer is **mammals**.

audioscript.text: And she found three places in the oceans which were hotspots.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And what these had in common was that these hotspots were all located at boundaries between ocean currents, and this seems to be the sort of place that has lots of the plankton that some of these species feed on.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So now people who want to protect the species that are endangered need to get as much information as possible.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: For example, there's an international project called the Census of Marine Life.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: They've been surveying oceans all over the world, including the Arctic.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: One thing they found there, which stunned other researchers, was that there were large numbers of species which live below the ice.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q36: The Census found species *'which live below the ice'*, sometimes under a 20-meter layer. The question asks where new species were living — under the **ice**. So the answer is **ice**.

audioscript.text: Sometimes under a layer up to 20 meters thick.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Some of these species had never been seen before.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: They've even found species of octopus living in these conditions.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And other scientists working on the same project, but researching very different habitats on the ocean floor have found large numbers of species congregating around volcanoes.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Attracted to them by the warmth and nutrients there.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: However, biologists still don't know how serious the threat to their survival is for each individual species.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So a body called the Global Marine Species Assessment is now creating a list of endangered species on land, so they consider things like the size of the population, how many members of one species there are in a particular place.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And then they look at their distribution in geographical terms, although this is quite difficult when you're looking at fish, because they're so mobile, and then thirdly, they calculate the rate at which the decline of the species is happening.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q37: The passage says they *'calculate the rate at which the decline of the species is happening'*. The question asks for the third factor they consider — the rate of **decline**. So the answer is **decline**.

audioscript.text: So far, only 1,500 species have been assessed, but they want to increase this figure to 20,000 for each one they assess.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: They use the data they collect on that species to produce a map showing its distribution.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q38: The passage says they *'use the data they collect on that species to produce a map showing its distribution'*. The question asks what they make for each species — a distribution **map**. So the answer is **map**.

audioscript.text: Ultimately, they will be able to use these to figure out not only where most species are located.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But also where they are most threatened.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So finally, what can be done to retain the diversity of species in the world's oceans?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Firstly, we need to set up more reserves in our oceans, places where marine species are protected.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: We have some, but not enough.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In addition, to preserve species such as leatherback turtles, which live out in the high seas, but have their nesting sites on the American coast.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: We need to create corridors for migration, so they can get from one area to another safely.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q39: The passage says *'we need to create corridors for migration'* so turtles can travel safely. The question asks what type of corridors to establish — **migration** corridors. So the answer is **migration**.

audioscript.text: As well as this, action needs to be taken to lower the levels of fishing quotas.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To prevent overfishing of endangered species. And finally, there's the problem of 'by-catch'.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: This refers to the catching of unwanted fish by fishing boats.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: They're returned to the sea, but they're often dead or dying.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: If these commercial fishing boats used equipment which was more selective, so that only the fish wanted for consumption were caught.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q40: The passage says equipment should be selective so *'only the fish wanted for consumption were caught'*. The question asks for the purpose of catching fish — for **consumption**. So the answer is **consumption**.

audioscript.text: This problem could be overcome.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So does anyone have any questions...
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 4.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.

utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: However, biologists still don't know how serious the threat to their survival is for each individual species.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: So a body called the Global Marine Species Assessment is now creating a list of endangered species on land, so they consider things like the size of the population, how many members of one species there are in a particular place.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: And then they look at their distribution in geographical terms, although this is quite difficult when you're looking at fish, because they're so mobile, and then thirdly, they calculate the rate at which the decline of the species is happening.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER
utterances.explain: Q37: The passage says they *'calculate the rate at which the decline of the species is happening'*. The question asks for the third factor they consider — the rate of **decline**. So the answer is **decline**.

utterances.text: So far, only 1,500 species have been assessed, but they want to increase this figure to 20,000 for each one they assess.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: They use the data they collect on that species to produce a map showing its distribution.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER
utterances.explain: Q38: The passage says they *'use the data they collect on that species to produce a map showing its distribution'*. The question asks what they make for each species — a distribution **map**. So the answer is **map**.

utterances.text: Ultimately, they will be able to use these to figure out not only where most species are located.

utterances.text: But also where they are most threatened.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: So finally, what can be done to retain the diversity of species in the world's oceans?
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: Firstly, we need to set up more reserves in our oceans, places where marine species are protected.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: We have some, but not enough.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: In addition, to preserve species such as leatherback turtles, which live out in the high seas, but have their nesting sites on the American coast.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: We need to create corridors for migration, so they can get from one area to another safely.

utterances.text: As well as this, action needs to be taken to lower the levels of fishing quotas.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: To prevent overfishing of endangered species. And finally, there's the problem of 'by-catch'.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: This refers to the catching of unwanted fish by fishing boats.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: They're returned to the sea, but they're often dead or dying.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: If these commercial fishing boats used equipment which was more selective, so that only the fish wanted for consumption were caught.
utterances.speaker: SPEAKER

utterances.text: This problem could be overcome.

audioscript.text: Good morning, Youth Council, Caroline speaking.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Oh, hello.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: I'm interested in standing for election to the Youth Council, and I was told to give you a call.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: That's good.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Could I have your name please?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Yes, it's Roger Brown.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Thank you.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: I'm Caroline, the Youth Council administrator.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: So do you know much about what the Council does, Roger?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: I've talked to Stephanie.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: I think she's the chair of the Council.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: That's right.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: And she told me a lot about it.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: How it's a way for young people to discuss local issues, for example.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: And make suggestions to the town council.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: That's what made me interested.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Fine, well let me take down some of your details.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Uh. First of all, how old are you?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: You know the Council is for young people aged from 13 to 18.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: I've just turned 18.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: And where do you live, Roger?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Uh. Well, that's a bit complicated.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: At the moment, I'm looking for a flat to rent here, so I'm in a hostel from Monday to Friday.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q1: The question asks where Roger stays during the week. He says *'I'm in a hostel from Monday to Friday'* — **'during the week'** means Monday to Friday. So the answer is **hostel**.

audioscript.text: I go back to my parents' place at the weekend.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: OK, so where's the best place to send you some information about the Council?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Oh, to my parents' address please.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: That's 17, Buckleigh Street - BUCKLEIGH.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q2: The question asks for the street name. Roger gives his address as *'17, Buckleigh Street'* and even spells it: *'BUCKLEIGH'*. So the answer is **Buckleigh**.

audioscript.text: Street, Stamford, Lincolnshire, though you don't really need the country.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Oh, I know Stamford.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: It's a lovely town.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: And what's the postcode?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: P, e, nine, seven, q, t.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q3: The question asks for the postcode. Roger says *'P, e, nine, seven, q, t'* — this is how you spell a postcode letter by letter and number by number. So the answer is **PE97QT**.

audioscript.text: Right, thank you.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Uh. So are you working here, or are you a student?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: I started studying at the university a couple of weeks ago, and I've got a part-time job for a few hours a week.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: What do you do?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Well, I've done several different things.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: I've just finished a short-term contract as a courier, and now I'm working as a waiter in one of the big hotels.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q4: The question asks about his part-time job. He says *'now I'm working as a waiter'* — **'now'** tells you this is his current job. So the answer is **waiter**.

audioscript.text: Uh huh. That can't leave you much time for studying.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Oh, it's not too bad.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: I manage to fit it all in.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: What are you studying?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: My ambition is to go into Parliament eventually, so my major subject is politics.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q5: The question asks for his major subject. Roger says *'my major subject is politics'* — this is a direct match. So the answer is **politics**.

audioscript.text: That's partly why I think the Youth Council is important, and want to be a part of it.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: And I suppose you're also taking a minor subject, aren't you?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: I know a lot of people study economics too.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: I chose history, to be honest, I'm not finding it as interesting as I expected.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Before you hear the rest of the phone call, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: OK, so with your studying and your part-time job, do you have time for any other interests or hobbies?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Well, I spend quite a lot of time cycling.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q6: The question asks about a hobby he does a lot. He says *'I spend quite a lot of time cycling'* — **'spend quite a lot of time'** means he does it often. So the answer is **cycling**.

audioscript.text: Both around town to get to university and to work, and also long distance from here to London for instance.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: That's pretty impressive, anything else?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: For relaxation, I'm also keen on the cinema.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q7: The question asks what else he is interested in. He says *'I'm also keen on the cinema'* — **'keen on'** means **'interested in'**. So the answer is **cinema**.

audioscript.text: I used to go at least once a week, but I can't manage to go so often now.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Right, are you sure you'll have enough time for the Youth Council?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Yes, I've worked out that I can afford to reduce my hours at work, and that will make the time.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: So, is there any particular aspect of the Youth Council's work that appeals to you, Roger?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Well, my sister is blind, so I'm particularly interested in working with disabled young people to try and improve the quality of their lives.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q8: The question asks who he wants to work with. He says he wants to work *'with disabled young people'* — **'young people who are disabled'** is the same idea. So the answer is **disabled**.

audioscript.text: That's great.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Well, the best way to get involved is to be nominated by some people who you know.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Right.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Can you tell me how to set about organizing that?
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: You should talk to Jeffrey, our Elections Officer.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: I can arrange a meeting in the Council office with him if you like.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Yes, please.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: He'll be here next Monday, if that suits you.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: That's the 14th, isn't it?
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Yes, I can manage late afternoon.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Would you like to suggest a time?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: He generally leaves around 5:30.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Well, would 4:30 be OK?
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q9: The question asks for the meeting time next Monday. Roger suggests *'would 4:30 be OK?'* and Caroline agrees. So the answer is **4:30**.

audioscript.text: My last class finishes at 4, so I'd have plenty of time to get to your office.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Right, that's fine.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Oh, and could I have a phone number we can contact you on?
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Yes, my mobile number is 07788136711.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER
audioscript.explain: Q10: The question asks for his mobile number. Roger says *'my mobile number is 07788136711'* — this is a direct answer. So the answer is **07788136711**.

audioscript.text: Thank you.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Well, we'll look forward to seeing you next week.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: Thanks very much.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Goodbye.
audioscript.speaker: ROGER

audioscript.text: Bye.
audioscript.speaker: CAROLINE

audioscript.text: That is the end of section 1.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

body.title: DESIGNING A PUBLIC BUILDING: THE TAYLOR CONCERT HALL

audioscript.text: Section 4.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You will hear part of a lecture to students of architecture about the design of a public building.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: We've been discussing the factors the architect has to consider when designing domestic buildings.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: I'm going to move on now to consider the design of public buildings.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And I'll illustrate this by referring to the new Taylor Concert Hall that's recently been completed here in the city.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So, as with a domestic building.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: When designing a public building, an architect needs to consider the function of the building.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Uh. For example, is it to be used primarily for entertainment?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Or for education, or for administration.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The second thing the architect needs to think about is the context of the building.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: This includes its physical location obviously, but it also includes the social meaning of the building.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q31: The question asks about the building's **physical and ___ context**. The passage says *'this includes its physical location obviously, but it also includes the **social** meaning of the building'*. So the missing word is **social**.

audioscript.text: How it relates to the people it's built for.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And finally, for important public buildings, the architect may also be looking for a central symbolic idea on which to base the design.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: A sort of metaphor for the building, and the way in which it is used.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Let's look at the new Taylor Concert Hall in relation to these ideas.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The location chosen was a site in a rundown district that has been ignored in previous redevelopment plans.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: It was occupied by a factory that had been empty for some years.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q32: The question says the site was a **disused ___**. The passage says the site *'was occupied by a **factory** that had been empty for some years'* — **'empty'** means **'disused'**. So the answer is **factory**.

audioscript.text: The whole area was some distance from the high-rise office blocks of the central business district and shopping center.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But it was only 1 km from the ring road.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The site itself was bordered to the north by a canal, which had once been used by boats bringing in raw materials when the area was used for manufacturing.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q33: The question asks what the building is **beside**. The passage says the site *'was bordered to the north by a **canal**'* — **'bordered by'** means **'beside'**. So the answer is **canal**.

audioscript.text: The architect chosen for the project was Tom Harrison.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: He found the main design challenge was the location of the site, in an area that had no neighboring buildings of any importance.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: To reflect the fact that the significance of the building in this quite run-down location was as yet unknown, he decided to create a building centered around the idea of a mystery.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Something whose meaning still has to be discovered.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: So, how was this reflected in the design of the building?
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Well, Harrison decided to create pedestrian access to the building.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And to make use of the presence of water on the site.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As people approach the entrance, they therefore have to cross over a bridge.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q34: The question says the building is **approached by a ___ for pedestrians**. The passage says *'as people approach the entrance, they therefore have to cross over a **bridge**'* — this is the pedestrian access. So the answer is **bridge**.

audioscript.text: He wanted to give people a feeling of suspense.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: As they see the building first from a distance, and then close up.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And the initial impression he wanted to create from the shape of the building as a whole was that of a box.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q35: The question asks about the building's **shape**. The passage says *'the initial impression he wanted to create from the shape of the building as a whole was that of a **box**'*. So the answer is **box**.

audioscript.text: The first side that people see, the southern wall, is just a high flat wall, uninterrupted by any windows.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Ha, this might sound off-putting.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: But it supports Harrison's concept of the building, that the person approaching is intrigued, and wonders what will be inside.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: And this flat wall also has another purpose.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: At night time, projectors are switched on, and it functions as a huge screen onto which images are projected.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q36: The question says one exterior wall acts as a **large ___**. The passage says *'it functions as a huge **screen** onto which images are projected'* — **'huge'** means **'large'**. So the answer is **screen**.

audioscript.text: The auditorium itself seats 1500 people.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The floor's supported by 10 massive pads.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: These are constructed from rubber, and so are able to absorb any vibrations from outside.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q37: The question asks what the huge pads are **made of**. The passage says *'these are constructed from **rubber**'* — **'constructed from'** means **'made of'**. So the answer is **rubber**.

audioscript.text: And prevent them from affecting the auditorium.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: The walls are made of several layers of honey colored wood, all sourced from local beech trees.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In order to improve the acoustic properties of the auditorium and to amplify the sound, they are not straight, they are curved.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q38: The question says the walls are **___ in shape**. The passage says *'they are not straight, they are **curved**'* — this directly describes the shape. So the answer is **curved**.

audioscript.text: The acoustics are also adjustable.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: According to the size of orchestra and the type of music being played, in order to achieve this, there are nine movable panels in the ceiling above the orchestra.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: Which are all individually motorized, and the walls also have curtains, which can be opened or closed to change the acoustics.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q39: The question says **ceiling panels and ___ on walls** adjust acoustics. The passage says *'the walls also have **curtains**, which can be opened or closed to change the acoustics'*. So the answer is **curtains**.

audioscript.text: The reaction of the public to the new building has generally been positive.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: However, the evaluation of some critics has been less enthusiastic.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER

audioscript.text: In spite of Harrison's efforts to use local materials, they criticize the style of the design as being international, rather than local, and say it doesn't reflect features of the landscape or society for which it is built.
audioscript.speaker: SPEAKER
audioscript.explain: Q40: The question asks about the **___ style** critics find inappropriate. The passage says critics *'criticize the style of the design as being **international**, rather than local'* — this is the style they dislike. So the answer is **international**.

audioscript.text: That is the end of Section 4.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.text: You now have half a minute to check your answers.
audioscript.speaker: ANNOUNCER

audioscript.speaker: MARTIN

audioscript.text: Oh, hello.
audioscript.speaker: SUE

audioscript.text: I saw a poster about free things to do in the area, and it said people should phone you for information.
audioscript.speaker: SUE

audioscript.text: I'm coming to Burnham with my husband and two children for a few days on June the 27th, or possibly the 28th, and I'd like some ideas for things to do on the 29th.
audioscript.speaker: SUE

audioscript.text: Yes, of course.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN

audioscript.text: OK.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN

audioscript.text: Then let's start with a couple of events especially for children.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN

audioscript.text: The art gallery is holding an event called Family Welcome that day, when there are activities and trails to use throughout the gallery.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN

audioscript.text: That sounds interesting.
audioscript.speaker: SUE

audioscript.text: What time does it start?
audioscript.speaker: SUE

audioscript.text: The gallery opens at 10, and the Family Welcome event runs from 10:30 until 2:00.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN
audioscript.explain: Q1: The question asks when the **Family Welcome** event *begins*. The passage says *'the Family Welcome event runs from 10:30 until 2:00'* — so it starts at **10:30 am**. The gallery opens at 10, but the event itself starts later. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: The gallery stays open until 5.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN

audioscript.text: And several times during the day, they're going to show a short film that the gallery has produced.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN

audioscript.text: It demonstrates how ceramics are made, and there'll be equipment and materials for children to have a go themselves.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN
audioscript.explain: Q2: The question asks what the film shown *now* is about. The passage says *'It demonstrates how ceramics are made'* — **'ceramics'** is the topic. audioscript.text: Last time they ran the event, there was a film about painting, which went down very well with the children, and they're now working on one about sculpture.
audioscript.speaker: MARTIN

audioscript.text: I like the sound of that.
audioscript.speaker: SUE

audioscript.text: And what other events happen in Burnham?

audioscript.text: You will hear a talk given by a woman called Shona Ferguson about changes in a town called Barford.

audioscript.text: First of all, let me thank you all for coming to this public meeting to discuss the future of our town.
audioscript.speaker: MAN

audioscript.text: Our first speaker is Shona Ferguson from Barford Town Council.
audioscript.speaker: MAN

audioscript.text: Shona.
audioscript.speaker: MAN

audioscript.text: Thank you.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: First I'll briefly give you some background information, then I'll be asking you for your comments on developments in the town.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Well, as you don't need me to tell you, Barford has changed a great deal in the last 50 years.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: These are some of the main changes.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: 50 years ago, buses linked virtually every part of the town and the neighboring towns and villages.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Most people use them frequently, but not now, because the bus companies concentrate on just the routes that attract most passengers.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q11: Many students think buses are empty because they are old, but the passage says *'replacing old uncomfortable buses with smart new ones has had little impact'* — so comfort is not the real reason. The key is that bus companies now *'concentrate on just the routes that attract most passengers'*, so **'parts of the town are no longer served by buses'**. This means there are **fewer routes** now. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: So parts of the town are no longer served by buses.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q11: Many students think buses are empty because they are old, but the passage says *'replacing old uncomfortable buses with smart new ones has had little impact'* — so comfort is not the real reason. The key is that bus companies now *'concentrate on just the routes that attract most passengers'*, so **'parts of the town are no longer served by buses'**. This means there are **fewer routes** now. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Even replacing old uncomfortable buses with smart new ones has had little impact on passenger numbers.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: It's sometimes said that bus fares are too high.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: But in relation to average incomes, fares are not much higher than they were 50 years ago.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Changes in the road network are affecting the town.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: The center was recently closed to traffic on a trial basis, making it much safer for pedestrians.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: The impact of this is being measured.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: The new cycle paths separating bikes from cars in most main roads are being used far more than was expected reducing traffic and improving air quality.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q12: The passage mentions three road changes, but only one is clearly successful. The bypass *'attempts... have failed'*, so **A** is wrong. The center closure is *'on a trial basis'* and its *'impact is being measured'* — we don't know if it helped. But the *'new cycle paths... are being used far more than was expected'*, reducing traffic and improving air. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: And although the council's attempts to have a bypass constructed have failed, we haven't given up hope of persuading the government to change its mind.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Shopping in the town center has changed over the years.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Many of us can remember when the town was crowded with people going shopping.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Numbers have been falling for several years.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Despite efforts to attract shoppers, for instance by opening new car parks.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Some people combine shopping with visits to the town's restaurants and cafes.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Most shops are small independent stores, which is good, but many people prefer to use supermarkets and department stores in nearby large towns, as there are so few well-known chain stores here.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q13: The problem is not parking — the town even *'opening new car parks'* to attract shoppers, so **A** is wrong. Restaurants and cafés exist, as *'some people combine shopping with visits'* to them, so **C** is wrong. The real issue is that *'there are so few well-known chain stores here'*, so people go to **nearby large towns** for supermarkets and department stores. **'Chain stores'** means **'major retailers'**. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: Turning now to medical facilities, the town is served by family doctors in several medical practices, fewer than 50 years ago, but each catering for far more patients.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Our hospital closed 15 years ago, which means journeys to other towns are unavoidable.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q14: The passage says *'Our hospital closed 15 years ago'*, which directly means there is **no hospital** now. It also says *'journeys to other towns are unavoidable'* for hospital care. The other options are wrong: medical practices are *'fewer than 50 years ago'*, not new ones planned, and there are *'more dentists than there used to be'*, not too few. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: On the other hand, there are more dentists than there used to be.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Employment patterns have changed along with almost everything else.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: The number of schools and colleges has increased, making that the main employment sector.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q15: The passage says *'The number of schools and colleges has increased, making that the main employment sector'*. **'That'** refers to **education** — schools and colleges. Manufacturing *'hasn't seen the decline'*, but it is not the largest. Services like website design have *'grown in importance'*, but are not the main sector. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Services such as website design and accountancy have grown in importance, and surprisingly perhaps, manufacturing hasn't seen the decline that has affected it in other parts of the country.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Now, I'll very quickly outline current plans for some of the town's facilities before asking for your comments.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: As you'll know, if you regularly use the car park at the railway station, it's usually full.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: The railway company applied for permission to replace it with a multi-storey car park.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: But that was refused.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: Instead, the company has bought some adjoining land, and this will be used to increase the number of parking spaces.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q16: The railway company wanted a multi-storey car park, but that was *'refused'*. Instead, they *'bought some adjoining land'* to *'increase the number of parking spaces'*. **'Increase the number'** means the car park will get bigger — it will be **expanded**. So the answer is **G**.

audioscript.text: The grand, the old cinema in the High Street, will close at the end of the year.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q17: The old cinema *'will close at the end of the year'* and *'reopen on a different site'*. **'Different site'** means a **new location**. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: And reopen on a different site.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q17: The old cinema *'will close at the end of the year'* and *'reopen on a different site'*. **'Different site'** means a **new location**. So the answer is **A**.

audioscript.text: You've probably seen the building under construction.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: The plan is to have three screens with fewer seats, rather than just the one large auditorium in the old cinema.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: I expect many of you shop in the indoor market. It's become more and more shabby-looking, and because of fears about safety, it was threatened with demolition.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: The good news is that it will close for 6 weeks to be made safe and redecorated, and the improved building will open in July.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q18: The indoor market was *'threatened with demolition'* because it was *'shabby-looking'* and unsafe. But now it will *'close for 6 weeks to be made safe and redecorated'*. **'RedeCorated'** and **'made safe'** means it will be **refurbished** — fixed up and improved. So the answer is **C**.

audioscript.text: Lots of people use the library,
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: including school and college students who go there to study.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: The council has managed to secure funding to keep the library open later into the evening, twice a week.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q19: The council got funding to *'keep the library open later into the evening, twice a week'*. **'Open later'** means its **opening hours are extended**. The plan to *'enlarge the building'* is *'by no means definite'*, so it is not expanded yet. So the answer is **B**.

audioscript.text: We would like to enlarge the building in the not too distant future, but this is by no means definite.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: There's no limit on access to the nature reserve on the edge of town.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: And this will continue to be the case.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA

audioscript.text: What will change though, is that the council will no longer be in charge of the area.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
audioscript.explain: Q20: The nature reserve will stay open with *'no limit on access'*, so hours don't change. But the council will *'no longer be in charge'* — instead, a *'national body'* will take responsibility. **'No longer be in charge'** means it will have **new management**. So the answer is **F**.

audioscript.text: Instead, it will become the responsibility of a national body that administers most nature reserves in the country.
audioscript.speaker: SHONA
